newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S MEAT-PROCESSORS EXPECT MEAT IMPORTS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S MEAT-PROCESSORS EXPECT MEAT IMPORTS.

text.p: Bulgaria's meat-processing association said on Thursday it expects pork shortages, due to unprecedented slaughter of swine caused by scarce fodder supplies.
"Bulgaria soon will have to import pork demand for this product rises during the winter and its supplies will fall," the association's chairman Ruman Kuzmanov told a news conference.
In a bid to reduce the animal count in their yards, farmers now sell swine at prices cheaper than the breeding cost.
Bulgaria's agriculture ministry decided last week to reduce swine breeding and poultry in order to leave fodder for winter feeding of more expensive cattle.
"The government should ease pork imports which now are burdened by a heavy import tax of $800 per tonne," Kuzmanov said.
Bulgaria in the throes of a grave grain crisis caused by excessive exports last year and poor harvest this year intends to import large quantities of grain and fodder. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
